references.text: Abraham fell on his face and laughed when God promised that Sarah would bear a son, reflecting Sarah's laughter and doubt in Genesis 18:13.
Sarah says that God has made laughter for her, and all who hear it will laugh with her—a fulfillment that looks back to her doubt and laughter in Genesis 18:13.
Paul describes Abraham's faith as not wavering even though he and Sarah's bodies were 'withered,' contrasting with Sarah's doubt about her old age in Genesis 18:13.
Sarah received power to conceive despite her advanced age because she held fast to the one who had given the promise—an overcoming of the doubt she showed in Genesis 18:13.
Zechariah doubted the angel's message that his elderly wife Elizabeth would bear a son, a parallel to Sarah's doubt about her age in Genesis 18:13.
The fulfillment of what was doubted in 18:13; Sarah's confirmation that God's promise of a child in old age was kept.
Contrast between human intervention due to doubt (16:2) and God's supernatural intervention despite doubt (18:13).
Prophecy and fulfillment: 18:13 expresses doubt about the promise, while 21:2 confirms that the promise was fulfilled at the right time.
A clear allusion in prophecy using Sarah's birth as proof of God's power to create life despite impossibility.
